What I do

One thing, done carefully: dining chair seats.

Reupholster drop-in seats

The old fabric and padding come off. New foam and batting go on, then your fabric, pulled tight and stapled by hand.

Repair seat frames

Cracked or broken seat boards get repaired and reinforced before any new fabric goes on, so the seat holds up.

Labor only, your fabric

You pick fabric you love and bring it, or I can pick it up. That keeps your cost down and the look entirely yours.

How it works

  1. Text me photos

    Send a few pictures of your chairs and tell me how many you have. I'll give you a quote and tell you how much fabric to buy.

  2. Choose your fabric

    Shop anywhere you like. RichTex Fabrics in Daphne is a great place to start, with a big selection in person.

  3. I rebuild each seat

    Old fabric off, bad foam out, repairs made, fresh foam and batting on, new fabric pulled tight and stapled down.

  4. Pickup or delivery

    Your chairs come back ready for dinner. Delivery in the area is available.

Questions

Do you supply the fabric?

You pick it. I charge for labor only, and you choose the fabric. That way you get exactly the look you want and avoid paying extra for materials. I handle the foam, batting and repairs.

How much fabric do I need?

Most dining chair seats take about half a yard each. Patterns that have to line up can need more. Text me a photo and the number of chairs, and I'll give you the exact amount before you buy.

What kinds of chairs do you work on?

Dining chairs with seats that lift out or are attached from underneath. That includes antique chairs. If you're not sure about yours, send a photo.

Can you fix a broken seat?

Yes. Cracked or broken seat boards can usually be repaired and reinforced before the new fabric goes on. I'll tell you what I see when I look at your photos.

How do I get a quote?

Text photos of your chairs to (865) 617-9660, or call. Tell me how many chairs you have and what fabric you're thinking of. Quotes are free.

Do you pick up and deliver?

Yes, in the area. Ask when you text and we'll work out what's easiest.
